ownership_reason: Only the gold sees the zone's previous transition and the offset in force before it; hops 1 and 2 compute the two estimates of the offset, hop 3 decides only when the estimates differ, and hop 4 only by the sign of the offset. For the trigger the estimates agree (+03:00 at 23:59:59.999Z) and the offset is positive, so the result is the gold's alone, and once an offset is returned no caller can tell whether the earlier or the later instant of a repeated local time was meant. The gold's javadoc promises, during an overlap where a local time occurs twice, the offset of the earlier instant; 02:59:59.999 occurs twice in Europe/Moscow on 2007-10-28 (22:59:59.999Z at +04:00 and 23:59:59.999Z at +03:00). The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's own javadoc (during a DST overlap the earlier instant); previousTransition of DateTimeZoneBuilder's precalculated and DST zones returns the transition minus one, which ZoneInfoCompiler.test verifies (trans - 1 != millis is reported as an error) and TestBuilder testReverseTransitions asserts (each result is the next transition minus one and carries the earlier offset); DateTimeZone.adjustOffset treats an overlap as the range from the transition instant given by nextTransition to transition + diff, end exclusive; the overlap tests test_getOffsetFromLocal_Moscow_Autumn_overlap_mins, test_DateTime_constructor_Moscow_Autumn and testDateTimeCreation_athens pass.
